candidates.planet: GJ 3634 candidate outer companion (RV drift, P>200d)
candidates.designation: Unnamed; Bonfils et al. 2011 describe 'the incomplete orbit of a companion of whose true nature is yet unknown'.
candidates.tier_reason: Backed only by an RV trend (owner's ruling: still a candidate, ambiguous). The drift is strongly detected - 1 planet + quadratic drift beats 1 planet alone by a Bayes factor ~5e5 - and Mignon et al. 2025 again need a quadratic long-term term for GJ 3634's HARPS RVs, but no orbit, no period and no mass have been measured, and the nature (planet, brown dwarf or star) is unknown. Gaia DR3 shows no NSS solution (RUWE 1.28).
candidates.orbit_flags: No orbit. Drift slope 21.77+/-0.77 m/s/yr and curvature -11.62+/-0.77 m/s/yr^2 (Table 2, global fit; MCMC in Sect. 4 gives 21.1+/-2.8 m/s/yr and -10.3+/-2.4 m/s/yr^2); 2009 RVs ~8 m/s below 2010. Sect. 5: period longer than the ~200 d 2010 span and a mass of order 32 M_E (~2 M_Nep) - the inequality sign is lost in the PDF text; read as a lower bound. 2009-2010 HARPS only (54 RVs).
candidates.reference: Bonfils X. et al. 2011, A&A 528, A111, arXiv:1102.1420, Sect. 4-5 and Table 2

candidates.designation: Unnamed; Murgas et al. 2024 say the RV residual trend 'may be caused by another massive object in the system'.
candidates.tier_reason: Backed only by an RV trend (owner's ruling: a candidate, ambiguous). The slope is formally significant (-0.22 +0.04/-0.05 m/s/d), but it comes from 22 CARMENES RVs over a 31 d baseline; the authors cannot limit the object's mass and explicitly say more RVs are needed to 'rule out certain stellar activity induced signal that may be the cause of this linear trend'. No follow-up published.
candidates.orbit_flags: No orbit, period or mass. Linear RV slope -0.22 (+0.04/-0.05) m/s/d fitted jointly with Wolf 327 b (Table 4); baseline only 31 d (Sect. 4.2 text: 'does not allow us to put limits on the mass of the object'). Could be activity. Note the nearby eclipsing binary TIC 4918919 is a separate star in the TESS aperture, not this companion.
candidates.reference: Murgas F. et al. 2024, A&A 684, A83, arXiv:2401.12150, Table 4 and Sect. 4.2, 6

candidates.designation: Unnamed 'single-transit candidate' (Serrano Bell et al. 2026, Sect. 3.7.1, Table A.2). The period is a posterior median from transit shape, not a measured period.
candidates.tier_reason: One transit-like event in TESS sector 79 (depth 0.21+/-0.03%, 2.2 h), checked against release notes and quality flags, but a single event: the authors say 'a single transit cannot validate a planet'. No TOI was issued for it and the expected RV (1-2.6 m/s) is below the current data's precision, so there is no independent support. Nothing argues against it either.

period_d.where: Table A.2 / Sect. 3.7.1: posterior median from a circular transit-shape fit with P>32.7 d imposed (log-uniform prior 32.7-2000 d); poorly constrained

candidates.orbit_flags: Single TESS transit at 3471.566 (+0.009/-0.006) TBJD; Rp/R*=0.045+/-0.003, b=0.8 (+0.1/-0.2), T14=2.9 h (Table A.2). Period only bounded (>32.7 d from absence of other transits); median 74 d. Mass NOT measured: the authors estimate ~5.8+/-1.2 M_E from an empirical M-R relation (Muller et al. 2024), expected K 1-2.6 m/s. TESS Cycle 9 re-observation expected (sector 118).

considered_not_added.name: Gl 725 B companion (Baize 1976, ~15 M_Jup, P~5.5 yr)
considered_not_added.reason: Brown-dwarf mass claimed (15 M_Jup > 13), and not confirmed: Kervella et al. 2019 and the SPIRou RVs show no such companion (as summarised in Ould-Elhkim et al. 2026, Sect. 2 and 5.3). Baize 1976 itself not opened.

considered_not_added.name: GJ 179 SRC P=3.95d (Butler et al. 2017)
considered_not_added.reason: Not a separate object: Tuomi et al. 2019 (App. A.10) show it is one of three HIRES aliases of the 3.48 d signal (reported here as GJ 179 c). Butler et al. themselves called it only a 'signal requiring confirmation'.

considered_not_added.name: GJ 436 c (UCF-1.01, P=1.365862 d, 0.66 R_E)
considered_not_added.reason: Refuted in practice though still 'Controversial' on exoplanet.eu and OEC: the discoverers' own HST/WFC3 follow-up contradicts the predicted transit at 3.1 sigma (Stevenson et al. 2014, arXiv:1410.0002), and Lanotte et al. 2014 (A&A 572, A73) re-reduce the same Spitzer data and find the transit not significant (1 sigma), attributing it to centring systematics (Sect. 4.2). Writer may prefer to file it on Rejected candidates.

considered_not_added.name: GJ 436 d (UCF-1.02, period unknown, 0.65 R_E)
considered_not_added.reason: Refuted in practice though still 'Controversial' on exoplanet.eu and OEC: single-epoch Spitzer event with no period (Stevenson et al. 2012, arXiv:1207.4245); Lanotte et al. 2014 find no evidence for any companion in the full Spitzer + HARPS analysis. Writer may prefer to file it on Rejected candidates.

considered_not_added.name: GJ 436 c (Ribas et al. 2008, ~5 M_E, P~5.2 d, 2:1 resonance)
considered_not_added.reason: Refuted: new RVs showed the signal spurious (Alonso et al. 2008, arXiv:0807.0235 abstract: 'Recent new radial velocities have deemed such signal spurious').

considered_not_added.name: GJ 436 EPOXI transit candidate (Ballard et al. 2010, 0.75 R_E)
considered_not_added.reason: Retracted by its authors: Warm Spitzer 4.5 um data 'rule out a transit at high confidence'; the earlier events were correlated noise (arXiv:1009.0755).

considered_not_added.name: GJ 436 outer perturber (ZLK companion, a<~6.8 AU, sub-Jovian)
considered_not_added.reason: Pure dynamical inference with no detected signal: arXiv:2604.09834 (2026) fit 20 yr of RVs + HGCA and 'do not detect an additional planet' (RV trend -0.0002 +/-0.0006 m/s/d, Table 1); they only bound where one could hide. JADE II (arXiv:2509.07938) likewise models a hypothetical companion.

considered_not_added.name: GJ 674 signal P~35d
considered_not_added.reason: Stellar rotation: attributed to activity by the discoverers (Bonfils et al. 2007) and by Tuomi et al. 2019 (36.65 d with photometric counterpart, App. A.41). Never proposed as a planet.

considered_not_added.name: GJ 393 signal P~730d (Tuomi et al. 2019)
considered_not_added.reason: Interpreted by Tuomi et al. 2019 themselves as a stellar activity cycle (counterparts in ASAS photometry at 720 d and HARPS S-index), App. A.24. Never proposed as a planet.

considered_not_added.name: GJ 393 signal P=317.2d (CARMENES DR1)
considered_not_added.reason: Listed in Ribas et al. 2023 Table A.2 as an 'unsolved' periodic signal (FAP 0.0051%), not a planet candidate; Amado et al. 2021 ascribe the long-period RV variability of Gl 393 to activity.

considered_not_added.name: GJ 422 signal P=6.671d (Tuomi et al. 2019)
considered_not_added.reason: Tuomi et al. 2019 (App. A.28) say the 6.6710 d signal and a 21.3 d local maximum were 'not significant enough to make the cut as planet candidates'; 'only suggestive evidence'. Not a published candidate.

considered_not_added.name: GJ 422 b at P=26.16d (Tuomi et al. 2014)
considered_not_added.reason: Same planet as the confirmed GJ 422 b: Feng et al. 2020 find 20.129 d stronger and consider the two signals related (Sect. on GJ 422). Tuomi et al. 2019 say the 26.1 d signal is not supported by newer HARPS data.
